newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-RESERVE HARDY LIFTS AUSTRALIA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-RESERVE HARDY LIFTS AUSTRALIA TO VICTORY.

text.p: Winger Mitch Hardy scored two tries in a memorable test debut during a 12-minute stint as a reserve as Australia overcame France 29-15 in the first rugby union test on Saturday.
Hardy transformed the match at the Sydney Football Stadium after taking the field as a temporary replacement for full-back Stephen Larkham mid-way through the second half.
But as soon as the ACT Brumbies winger scored his second try he was pulled out of the action by Wallaby coach Greg Smith to allow Larkham's return after treatment for a facial injury.
Those two tries broke a 15-15 deadlock after France fought their way back into the game with two tries either side of half-time from winger Philippe Bernat-Salles and centre Thomas Castaignede.
Australia scored their first 15 points through the boot of captain and lock John Eales, who landed five penalties.
But the victory, in front of a crowd of 31,572, was fully earned by the Wallabies, who produced a stirring second half performance after trailing 6-8 at halftime.
Hardy scored his first try when he took a short pass from scrum-half George Gregan before beating two defenders and diving over near the posts in the 68th minute.
Three minutes later, Hardy used his soccer skills to twice kick the ball forward off the ground after a break by right-winger Joe Roff.
Hardy beat the French defenders in a race to the ball and touched down with his finger tips.
After a disjointed start to the match, France gradually found their stride and their growing confidence was rewarded when they scored the opening try after 36 minutes.
Ignoring the chance of a simple penalty in front of the posts, captain Abdel Benazzi opted for a quick tap to maintain the pressure.
When Australia infringed again, centre Thomas Castaignede quickly released fly-half David Aucagne, whose clever kick was touched down by Bernat-Salles in the corner.
Centre Richard Dourthe, who earlier landed a penalty, missed the conversion.

Castaignede brought the tourists back on level terms when he completed a flowing move from deep within the French half after fine work from full-back Jean-Luc Sadourny and Aucagne. Dourthe kicked the conversion.

France - 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Philippe Bernat-Salles, 13-Richard Dourthe, 11-David Venditti (Sebastien Viars, 39th); 10-David Aucagne, 9-Philippe Carbonneau; 8-Fabien Pelous, 7-Olivier Magne, 6-Abdel Benazzi (captain), 5-Olivier Merle, 4-Olivier Brouzet, 3-Christian Califano, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Franck Tournaire.

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham (Mitch Hardy, 60th); 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-Pat Howard, 11-Joe Roff; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan; 8-Daniel Manu, 7-David Wilson (Troy Coker, 51st), 6-Brett Robinson, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-David Giffen, 3-Ewen McKenzie, 2-Marco Caputo, 1-Richard Harry.
